## 5. The ordinary single-band comparator is stronger for the currently demonstrated local CZ task

Use one semi-infinite bath with band `[0,2]`, keep both memories at energy 3, and couple both memories equally to its endpoint with amplitude `sqrt(3/2) g`. The bright memory mode then has endpoint coupling `sqrt3 g`; the dark mode is uncoupled. The total squared memory-bath coupling is

\[
\|v_+\|^2+\|v_-\|^2=3g^2,
\]

exactly matching the source's `2g^2 + g^2`. The leading pair bath occupation is also the same, `3bg^2`, and the leading one-particle exchange splitting has the same magnitude, `3ag^2`.

The general hard-core interaction formula gives

\[
\boxed{\chi_{\rm one\ band}=+9abg^4+O(g^6)
=+1.492267835786\ldots\,g^4+O(g^6).}\tag{7}
\]

Its magnitude is **three times** the source's `3abg^4`. This pair is isolated from the entire two-particle continuum, not only a symmetry sector. Both memories remain hard-core; no Kerr interaction is inserted. The same adiabatic/echo logic applies in the declared model. The sign difference has no cost for a CZ phase modulo `2pi`; an upper single band gives the opposite sign if needed.

The result is also visible directly inside the source's existing tunability formula. At fixed `t^2+s^2`, the magnitude of

\[
\chi(t,s)=-8ab\,ts(t^2+s^2)+O((|t|+|s|)^6)
\]

is maximized at `t=s` or `t=-s`. For `t=s=(sqrt3/2)g`, one parity coupling vanishes and the remaining one has magnitude `sqrt3 g`. The unused parity continuum can be retained as a spectator, making the same operative single-band mechanism globally embedded, or removed, leaving an ordinary globally bound gate. Thus global embedding itself does not supply the demonstrated interaction advantage.

This comparison matches total coupling strength, leading dressing population, leading exchange magnitude, locality at the same endpoint, and the hard-core resource. It does not establish an all-platform or all-noise dominance theorem. A use requiring the otherwise available global scattering channels could change the comparison, but no such extra capability has yet been acquired for this construction.

## A stronger ordinary local-gate comparator

For the local same-end two-memory gate, global embedding itself provides no demonstrated performance resource. At fixed total squared endpoint coupling

\[
P=c_+^2+c_-^2=2(t^2+s^2),
\]

(6) yields |chi|=abP|Delta|+O(P^3)<=abP^2+O(P^3). The leading interaction is maximized by one accessible band, c_-=0 or c_+=0.

With c_-=0 (t=s), the lower band is exactly decoupled from both memories. Exchanging the two bath rails while leaving EACH memory fixed is conserved even with unequal memory frequencies. Equivalently the lower-band excitation number is conserved and remains zero from a memory-only input.

In this accessible subsystem the two-excitation continuum begins near energy 7 (one memory plus an upper-band photon); the pair remains near 6. For sufficiently small coupling and |epsilon|<1 with an adequate gap margin, the pair is an ordinary isolated bound state. Static memory imbalance cannot radiate into the lower band at any order. This requires symmetric coupling to the two rails and preserved bath bands, but does not require memory-exchange symmetry.

The preserved calibration uses P=3g^2 and has |chi|=3abg^4+O(g^6). The single-band comparator at the same P gives |chi|=9abg^4+O(g^6): three times larger at leading order, with no radiation caused by D.

Thus the two-band embedded-pair architecture has no established local-gate advantage over this equally resourced band-gap comparator. It remains a valid interacting embedded eigenstate construction. A practical advantage requires a further task or constraint genuinely demanding both bands or globally gapless accessible modes.

Neither architecture resolves rail disorder, external electromagnetic modes, thermal occupation, control noise, or finite-time loading cost.

## F. Repairs and ordinary comparator retain their costs

Sequential activation is an exact commutator statement for the stated density
coupling. With each spectator bath coupling exactly zero,its memory occupation
commutes with the full Hamiltonian and its empty bath remains empty. Conditioning
on spectator occupations shifts the active memory frequency by the sum of the
density couplings. Its gap must remain open. Spectator superpositions retain
conditional phases. Imperfect switch-off or exchange couplers are not covered.

For bounded local deviation spectra in [-D_j,-d_j] union{0} union[d_j,D_j],
d_j>sum_(i<j)D_i makes the largest-index nonzero deviation dominate every
earlier possible cancellation. The product gap is at least the minimum of
those strict margins. B_j>6 sum_(i<j)B_i is the source's sufficient specialization;
a geometric ratio>7 pays exponential frequency span. It is not an optimum or
a rule for unbounded non-RWA parity sectors.

For the original local gate,fix P=c_+^2+c_-^2=3g^2. The governing source's
general leading functional is chi=-ab P(c_+^2-c_-^2)+O(g^6). Its calibrated
two-band case has |chi|=3abg^4; the one-accessible-band endpoints give 9abg^4.
Leading dressing bP and exchange magnitude aP match. The upper-band choice
has an exactly invariant empty lower band even under memory imbalance,because
both memories couple only to the upper rail combination. At g=0 and |epsilon|<1,
the accessible two-particle complement starts above the pair by at least
1-|epsilon|; a strict small-coupling margin retains this isolated branch.
This accepts the leading mathematical comparator and this static-detuning
subspace statement,not faster hardware or full-noise dominance. The unbalanced
coupling example in cooperative section10 has a different P and is not the
matched factor-three comparison.
